about: The only facts a Short may state. A script line lists the IDs it uses in "facts".
status: confirmed (may be stated), reported (may be stated only in its safe wording), unverified (may not be used).
Only the owner changes a status or gives a new fact as confirmed. Claude adds new facts as unverified and never marks one confirmed on its own.
safe_wording is how to say it on screen and in the voice. also_ok lists other wordings that are just as safe.
Every number a line says or shows must be in the wording of a fact that line lists (for a reported fact: in its safe wording).
source is the main link and more_sources lists the others that say the same.
time_sensitive is true for a fact that can change from day to day (launch-week dates, times and sizes). checked_on is the day it was last read against its sources, as YYYY-MM-DD.

A script that uses a time_sensitive fact checked more than 3 days ago is refused by make_short.py, until the fact is checked again and its checked_on is set to that day (or the owner passes --allow-stale).

facts.claim: GTA 6 launches 19 Nov 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
facts.safe_wording: GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
facts.note: The summary of Rockstar's Newswire post of 3 Nov 2026 says "when it launches on November 19".

facts.claim: Digital pre-load on PS5 started at midnight local time on 10 Nov 2026.
facts.safe_wording: digital pre-load on PS5 started at midnight local time on November 10
facts.note: Until 2026-11-12 this fact said November 12, which was Rockstar's June date. The owner corrected it. The title of Rockstar's post is "Grand Theft Auto VI Pre-Load Begins on November 10". Rockstar's own pages would not open for Claude on 2026-11-12 (the Newswire page loads only its title and summary, the support pages time out), so the wording was read on the news sites listed.

facts.claim: Digital pre-load on Xbox Series X|S opened for everyone at the same moment, reported as 12 a.m. GMT on 10 Nov 2026 (the evening of 9 Nov in the Americas).
facts.safe_wording: on Xbox, pre-load reportedly opened at midnight GMT on November 10
also_ok: on Xbox, pre-load reportedly opened at 12 a.m. GMT on November 10
on Xbox it reportedly opened at midnight GMT on November 10
facts.note: The owner said to keep this reported unless Rockstar's own wording is found. timesaver.gg prints it as a quote from Rockstar's support page: "On XBOX Series X|S, digital pre-load begins globally at 12 a.m. GMT on November 10, 2026." Rockstar's own pages would not open for Claude on 2026-11-12 (the Newswire page loads only its title and summary, the support pages time out), so the wording was read on the news sites listed. If the owner sees that sentence on Rockstar's page, this can be confirmed. The also_ok wordings were added by Claude and keep the word "reportedly".

facts.claim: Rockstar's update of 3 Nov 2026 moved digital pre-load forward from November 12 to November 10.
facts.safe_wording: Rockstar moved digital pre-load forward from November 12 to November 10
facts.note: Given by the owner on 2026-11-12. TechPowerUp: digital pre-orders start "on November 10, instead of the November 12 date announced back in June".

facts.claim: November 12 is the date for boxed (retail) copies, which hold a download code and no disc. It is not the digital pre-load date.
facts.safe_wording: boxed copies arrive in shops from November 12
facts.note: Given by the owner on 2026-11-12. It replaces the unverified fact code-in-box-nov-12. TechPowerUp says the date "reportedly still stands" and digitbin says copies are "expected at retailers from November 12".

facts.claim: The pre-load needs up to 212 GB of free space, depending on the device. Rockstar gave no figure for each console.
facts.safe_wording: up to 212 GB of free space
facts.note: Given by the owner on 2026-11-12. Rockstar's wording as the news sites quote it: "up to 212 GB of available space depending on your device". It replaces ps5-download-size ("over 200 GB", reported) and ps5-size-212-gb (unverified); neither figure was only about PS5. "gigabytes" and "gigs" count as GB.

facts.claim: Rockstar says GTA 6 releases at midnight local time on 19 Nov 2026 in all regions, on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
facts.safe_wording: Rockstar says GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time on November 19
also_ok: unlocks at midnight local time on November 19
facts.note: Given by the owner on 2026-11-12; until then this fact was reported ("expected to unlock"). timesaver.gg and Forbes quote Rockstar's support page: "Grand Theft Auto VI will release midnight local time on November 19, 2026, in all regions for both PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S." Rockstar's own pages would not open for Claude on 2026-11-12 (the Newswire page loads only its title and summary, the support pages time out), so the wording was read on the news sites listed. See us-store-eastern-midnight for what "local" may mean in the US. The also_ok wordings were added by Claude.

facts.claim: GTA 6 has six wanted stars, one more than GTA 5's five. Rockstar's own Extended Look presentation (Netflix, 27 Aug 2026) shows the wanted HUD with six stars.
facts.safe_wording: GTA 6 has six wanted stars, one more than GTA 5's five
also_ok: In GTA 5, five stars. In GTA 6, six.
facts.note: Status set by Claude under the owner's 2026-11-13 rule (confirmed = 2+ independent sites citing Rockstar's own presentation); the owner may downgrade it. Four sites, all read in full on 2026-11-13, say Rockstar's Extended Look (Netflix, 27 Aug 2026) shows six stars: Shacknews (27 Aug), Beebom (28 Aug), KeenGamer (28 Aug: "The Extended Look confirms that six Wanted stars return in GTA 6"), SVG (27 Aug). Not used: how many stars the chase reached (Game Informer says four of six, Engadget says six visible: the outlets disagree). Rockstar's own pages had nothing on this.

facts.claim: Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson told IGN that a crime must be witnessed by someone, or an alarm set off, before it is reported to the police.
facts.safe_wording: Rockstar says a crime needs a witness, or an alarm, before police hear about it
also_ok: Rockstar says police only hear about a crime from a witness or an alarm
facts.note: Status set by Claude under the owner's 2026-11-13 rule; the owner may downgrade it. WEAKEST of the confirmed calls: it rests on second-hand quotes, because IGN's own preview and interview would not open for Claude (ign.com is blocked). SVG quotes Nelson via IGN: "requires that someone witness the crime, or an alarm needs to be set off"; Beebom attributes the same to Nelson via IGN; KeenGamer says IGN reported that "a crime must be reported" and that witnesses and alarms can inform police. Vice adds that a stolen car's tracker can also report a crime (not used).

facts.claim: A hollow wanted star means a crime has been reported, but the police have no description of the suspect.
facts.safe_wording: a hollow star reportedly means a crime was reported but police have no description of you
facts.note: Reported, not confirmed: Vice (5 Sep 2026) takes it from creators who visited Rockstar North in July (TGG, TroisCouleurs). GameRant repeats Vice, so it is not independent. Gamer.org, Beebom and GTABase give the same meaning but name no source. No page from Rockstar itself says it.

facts.claim: A solid white wanted star means the police have a direct line of sight on the player.
facts.safe_wording: a solid white star reportedly means police can see you right now
facts.note: Reported, same sourcing as wanted-hollow-star. Vice: "Solid white stars mean the police have a direct line of sight on the player". "Can see you right now" is Claude's plain-English rewording of direct line of sight.

facts.claim: A red wanted star means the player has technically escaped the police but is still inside the active search area.
facts.safe_wording: a red star reportedly means you escaped but police are still searching
facts.note: Reported, same sourcing as wanted-hollow-star. Vice: "Red wanted stars mean players have technically escaped the police but remain inside the active search area."

facts.claim: A Heat system shows small icons under the wanted stars that tell the player what the police know about them (CCTV footage, description, outfit, weapons, getaway vehicle).
facts.safe_wording: small icons under the stars reportedly show what police know about you
facts.note: Reported. Vice: "A new Heat system works alongside GTA 6's traditional wanted stars and tracks exactly what the police know". SVG credits IGN for the camera, single-person and clothes-hanger icons; Beebom says the Extended Look and Rob Nelson show indicators for appearance, clothing, vehicle and CCTV. IGN itself was not readable. Sites disagree on the exact list of icons, so no script may name more than "what police know".

facts.claim: The police can know what the player is wearing and which getaway vehicle they are in, so changing clothes or switching vehicles can matter.
facts.safe_wording: police can reportedly know your outfit and your getaway car
facts.note: Reported. Vice: heat indicators show "descriptions of the characters' appearances and outfits" and "details about their getaway vehicle". SVG quotes Rob Nelson via IGN that the police "will still know what you are wearing" after a haircut. KeenGamer (citing IGN): "Masks, changing clothes and switching vehicles can therefore become useful escape strategies." The car icon itself is only SVG's guess ("presumably"); this fact does not rely on it.

facts.claim: A camera icon under the wanted stars tells the player the police have CCTV footage of them.
facts.safe_wording: a camera icon reportedly means police have CCTV footage of you
facts.note: Reported, added for a possible evidence Short (not used in Short 1). SVG credits IGN: "a camera icon which alerts you to the fact that police have video footage of you from CCTV". Vice: indicators show "whether police have CCTV footage". IGN itself was not readable. Nothing found says what a camera records beyond this.

facts.claim: Players can destroy CCTV footage; in a store robbery Rockstar showed press, the developer destroyed the CCTV footage while searching for a safe code.
facts.safe_wording: you can reportedly destroy CCTV footage
facts.note: Reported, added for a possible evidence Short. Vice (a creator's account of a Rockstar demo): "The developer knocked out the clerk without killing her, destroyed the CCTV footage and searched for a safe code." Gamer.org says players can "potentially" destroy security footage; GameRant repeats Vice.

facts.claim: Splitting Jason and Lucia up during an escape can remove an entire wanted star.
facts.safe_wording: splitting up Jason and Lucia can reportedly remove a wanted star
facts.note: Reported, added for a possible evidence Short. Vice: "Splitting Jason and Lucia up during an escape can reportedly remove an entire wanted star." Gamer.org says it can "reportedly reduce the police response". Vice and GameRant are one chain of sourcing.

facts.claim: Masks, changing clothes and switching vehicles can become useful ways to escape the police.
facts.safe_wording: masks, new clothes and a new car reportedly help you escape
facts.note: Reported, added for a possible evidence Short. KeenGamer (citing IGN's preview): "Masks, changing clothes and switching vehicles can therefore become useful escape strategies." Vice lists changing clothes and switching vehicles but not masks. Beebom's mask advice is the writer's own, so it does not count. Only one independent site names masks.
